Run SQL once per existing environment; fresh databases skip it.

eli5.text: If you manage your own copy of the tool, the command you run to update your database layout has changed from a quick-fix mode to a proper migration mode. The old method adjusted the database directly without keeping a record, while the new method logs each change so it can be replayed or reversed. To bridge the gap, a one-time setup script tells the system that all previous changes have already been applied, so only future changes will run.

ai.title: CLI wait list UX: Tab/arrow key cycling, fixed-width hints, muted wait
ai.summary: Model selector keyboard shortcuts change from number keys (1-9) to Tab/Shift+Tab and Left/Right arrow cycling. Up/Down keys are intentionally ignored to avoid conflicts with other vertical UI. Trailing hints ('N ahead', 'No wait', tagline) are padded to a fixed width computed via useMemo to prevent button resizing as queue depth changes. Waiting room screen 'Wait' label and value now render in muted foreground instead of primary, reducing visual noise.

eli5.text: When you're waiting in the Freebuff queue (the spot that shows you're in line for a busy AI model), you'll now switch between model buttons with Tab, Shift+Tab, and the Left/Right arrow keys instead of pressing number keys, Up/Down won't accidentally change your selection. The "N ahead", "No wait", and tagline text next to each model stays the same width as the numbers tick down, so buttons no longer shuffle around and jump. The "Wait" label and your wait time on the waiting room screen are now shown in the same muted color as the rest of the labels, so they don't draw extra attention against the other info.

ai.title: Add two-step keyboard navigation to model selector
ai.summary: The CLI model selector now uses two-step keyboard navigation: Tab/arrow keys move a focus highlight, while Enter/Space commits the model switch. This prevents accidental queue position loss when navigating past the currently selected model. Mouse clicks remain one-step. Implemented in `cli/src/components/freebuff-model-selector.tsx` by separating `focusedId` from `selectedModel` state.

eli5.text: When you're picking which assistant model to wait in line for, keyboard users now use two steps: arrow keys move a highlight to preview a model, and Enter then confirms the switch. This matters because switching lines costs you your spot in the old line, the system re-queues you at the back of the new model's line, so this preview step keeps you from accidentally losing your place just by tabbing too far. Mouse clicks still switch immediately as before. You'll notice a separate highlight that follows your arrow keys without triggering a change until you press Enter.

ai.title: Freebuff 0.0.42 ships Drizzle migrations, Tab nav, and two-step model
ai.summary: Version 0.0.42 bundles changes across the CLI and web server since 0.0.41, led by switching the internal db:migrate script to drizzle-kit migrate so existing environments skip prior push-managed migrations via a seeded __drizzle_migrations journal entry. The CLI model selector now uses two-step keyboard navigation (Tab/arrows to focus, Enter/Space to commit), Tab/Shift+Tab and Left/Right arrow cycling replacing number keys, fixed-width trailing hints, and a muted 'Wait' label in the waiting room. The web LLM API gains a minimax/minimax-m2.7 Fireworks deployment mapping, and an internal long-test script gains matching cost and deployment config.
ai.evidence: Commit 4c96ed75 modifies only freebuff/cli/release/package.json, bumping the version field from 0.0.41 to 0.0.42. Analysis notes classify it as a release-bump with +1/-1 stats, and the release instructions direct summarizing shipped user-visible changes rather than the version change itself.

eli5.text: Freebuff 0.0.42 adds a new AI model named Minimax M2.7, makes the model picker easier to use with keyboard arrows, and cleans up the sign-in waitlist screen. When you open the model selection menu, you can now use Tab, Shift-Tab, and the left and right arrow keys to highlight models, then press Enter or Space to switch, which prevents accidentally skipping your current choice. The waiting room for the invite-only sign-in list now uses softer colors for the Wait label and number, and the position hints below each option keep a steady width so the buttons do not jump around as your spot in line changes. On the server side, the database setup now runs migrations in a safer, more structured way that skips work already completed and only runs once per existing account. Upgrading gives you access to the newer Minimax model faster and makes choosing and switching between models feel smoother, while the waitlist interface looks calmer and behaves more predictably while you wait.

ai.title: Model tagline moves inline in CLI selector
ai.summary: Tagline rendering shifts to an inline span next to the model name in cli/src/components/freebuff-model-selector.tsx, removing it from the trailing hint slot. The hintWidth calculation drops the max(tagline.length) term, fixing the slot to 'No wait' or '999 ahead' widths. Affects the CLI freebuff model picker surface.

eli5.text: The assistant picks a model in the command-line menu. Previously each model showed a short description as a trailing hint on the right edge, which forced that hint column to be wide enough for the longest description (so the buttons jumped around less, but left extra blank space for short descriptions). Now that same description appears right next to the model name, and the trailing hint only carries the queue status, so it is fixed to the width needed for 'No wait' or '999 ahead' and no longer stretches to fit any description. You would notice the right-side hint is more predictable and tighter, and the model descriptions now look like 'DeepSeek V3 · Powerful reasoning model' inline instead of sitting in the trailing column.

ai.title: Per-model active session counts in admission logs
ai.summary: Admission tick logs per-model active session counts via new `activeCountsByModel` store function replacing global `activeCount`. Adds SQL `GROUP BY` on `freeSession.model` for single-query bucketed reads. Updates `AdmissionTickResult` interface and `AdmissionDeps` to carry `Record<string, number>` instead of scalar. Affects `web/src/server/free-session/admission.ts` and `store.ts`; log aggregator now receives `activeCountByModel` metric alongside existing `queueDepthByModel`.

eli5.text: The waiting-room system now logs how many people are actually using each AI assistant model at the same time, rather than a single total number. Previously, all models’ active users were lumped together into one count, making it hard to tell which assistants were busy. You wouldn’t notice this directly unless you watch the server logs or dashboards, but from now on those monitoring tools will show a per-model traffic chart that updates every few seconds, so developers can spot which models are overcrowded. This is live today and affects how the system watches and balances load behind the scenes.

eli5.text: When you open the model selector in a narrow terminal window, the two model buttons now stack on top of each other instead of squeezing side by side. The program checks how wide your screen is and how long each button's text is, and if they wouldn't both fit comfortably, it switches from a horizontal to a vertical layout. Up and down arrow keys now move the highlight between the buttons, so you can navigate without accidentally leaving the selection screen.

ai.title: Freebuff 0.0.43 release packages CLI selector refinements
ai.summary: Version bumped to 0.0.43 in `freebuff/cli/release/package.json`, bundling changes shipped since 0.0.42. The CLI freebuff model picker now renders the model tagline as an inline span next to the name (cli/src/components/freebuff-model-selector.tsx), freeing the trailing hint slot to fixed 'No wait' or '999 ahead' widths; the picker also stacks buttons vertically on narrow terminals via `useTerminalDimensions` and accepts Up/Down arrows for focus movement. On startup the CLI now GET-probes queue status before joining, surfacing live `queueDepthByModel` counts on a pre-chat landing screen instead of a shimmer; `switchFreebuffModel` was renamed to `joinFreebuffQueue` in cli/src/hooks/use-freebuff-session.ts and `PollController.setHasPosted` was removed. On the web side, the admission tick now reports per-model active session counts through a new `activeCountsByModel` store function (GROUP BY on `freeSession.model`) replacing the global `activeCount`, with `AdmissionDeps` carrying `Record<string, number>` alongside the existing `queueDepthByModel` metric.
ai.evidence: Single hunk in `freebuff/cli/release/package.json` changes the `version` field from `0.0.42` to `0.0.43`.

eli5.text: Freebuff 0.0.43 improves how you pick AI models in the terminal and makes the waiting experience clearer. The model selector now shows each model's tagline directly next to its name, so you get a quick hint about what it is without extra clutter. When your terminal is narrow, the model buttons stack vertically instead of squishing horizontally, and you can use the Up and Down arrow keys to move between them easily. Before joining the queue, the app now checks the server first and shows you how many people are ahead of you per model on a landing screen, replacing the old spinning 'Joining...' message. Session and admission logging now tracks active sessions by model, which helps keep usage fair and queue lengths transparent. Overall, the release makes choosing a model faster, navigating on smaller screens smoother, and waiting less of a mystery.

ai.title: evictBanned frees banned users' freesession slots each admission tick
ai.summary: Adds evictBanned to web/src/server/free-session/store.ts, deleting free_session rows where the linked user is banned. Runs in parallel with sweepExpired in runAdmissionTick (web/src/server/free-session/admission.ts) so slots freed this tick admit queued users immediately. Bans via admin UI, direct SQL, or Stripe webhook previously left users holding slots until expires_at. AdmissionTickResult now carries evictedBanned count, logged under freebuff_waiting_room metric.

eli5.text: When the system checks who gets to use the free service, it now also kicks out anyone who has been banned, freeing up that spot right away for someone waiting in line. Previously, a banned person kept holding their slot until it naturally expired, blocking others even though they were no longer allowed to use the service. If you watch the queue move, banned users disappear and new users get admitted faster within the same check cycle. This is live today as part of the regular admission process.

ai.title: CLI uses hardware fingerprint for login
ai.summary: CLI login flow now uses a stable hardware-based fingerprint via `node-machine-id` instead of random IDs. `getFingerprintId()` caches the result process-wide and falls back to legacy random generation if hardware hashing fails. Covers `cli/src/utils/fingerprint.ts`, `login-modal.tsx`, `init-app.ts`, and `login-store.ts`. Login polling gates on `fingerprintId` to ensure consistent auth state.

eli5.text: When you log into the assistant from the command-line tool, it now identifies your specific computer by its hardware instead of by a random, throwaway label that changed every time you started the program. This means your login session is recognized on the same machine later, so you won't be asked to log in again unnecessarily, even if you close and reopen the command line. If the hardware lookup fails for any reason (like some shared or virtual machines), it safely falls back to the old random method, so you can still log in normally.

ai.title: Instant-admit free sessions when below per-model capacity
ai.summary: Adds instant-admit logic to `requestSession` in `web/src/server/free-session/public-api.ts`. New joiners skip the FIFO queue if the model's active session count is below a configured `INSTANT_ADMIT_CAPACITY` (e.g., 50 for `z-ai/glm-5.1`, 200 for `minimax/minimax-m2.7`). Backpressure engages only when this threshold is reached. Includes new store functions `activeCountForModel` and `promoteQueuedUser` to handle the state transition.

eli5.text: When someone asks to join a free session for a specific AI model, the system now checks how many people are already using that model. If the number is below the model's set limit (for example, 50 for one model or 200 for another), the new person skips the waiting line and starts right away. Only when that limit is reached does the queue kick in. If two people ask at the exact same moment and both see room, the system allows both in even if it slightly exceeds the limit, since the numbers are chosen with extra space to handle that.

This change affects users who are using the freebuff mode of the CLI, and it is live today as of the current release.

ai.title: Freebuff 0.0.44 release ships instant-admit, banned-slot eviction
ai.summary: Freebuff ships version 0.0.44, aggregating changes since 0.0.43 across the CLI and web server packages. Free sessions now instant-admit joiners below a per-model capacity in `web/src/server/free-session/public-api.ts`, while `evictBanned` in `web/src/server/free-session/store.ts` frees banned users' slots each admission tick in parallel with `sweepExpired`. The CLI returns users to the model picker after a session ends via `returnToFreebuffLanding` replacing re-queue logic, login now uses a stable hardware fingerprint `getFingerprintId()` backed by `node-machine-ID`, and the minimax/minimax-m2.7 Fireworks deployment mapping was re-disabled in `web/src/lib/llm-api/fireworks-config.ts`. All changes are packaged through `freebuff/cli/release/package.json`.
ai.evidence: The diff in `freebuff/cli/release/package.json` bumps the `version` field from `0.0.43` to `0.0.44`, a single-line release-bump commit on 2026-04-21, with the accompanying release notes enumerating the six user-facing changes since 0.0.43.

eli5.text: Freebuff 0.0.44 improves how you connect to AI models when free slots are available, and it stops banned users from holding spots that other people need. When demand is low, new users now join instantly instead of waiting in a first-in-line queue, so you get started right away as long as the model isn't already full. If someone gets banned while using a free session, their slot is now removed immediately during routine cleanup, freeing that space so queued users can move in right away. The program also identifies your computer by a stable hardware fingerprint when you log in, so signing in works more reliably across restarts and isn't confused by random temporary IDs. Finally, ending a session now takes you back to the model picker screen where you can choose what to use next, rather than dropping you straight back into a waiting line for the same model you just left. Upgrading means faster access during light usage, cleaner handling of disruptive users, and clearer navigation when you want to switch models.
